claim: The aircraft tracked over Sonora, California is identified correctly. FAA registry N904DK is a Beech C90A King Air, serial LJ-1089, built 1984, a twin turboprop registered to Aerolease LLC at 3802 20th St N, Fargo, North Dakota — the same address as Weather Modification LLC, a cloud-seeding contractor in business since 1966. The aircraft holds a Standard-Restricted airworthiness certificate whose approved operations are listed as "Weather Control, Aerial Advertising, Agriculture and Pest Control." A restricted-category certificate in the Weather Control class is the FAA's designation for an aircraft equipped to seed clouds.

notes: Registry page pulled directly and parsed; registry.faa.gov 403s the fetcher on a plain request. Recorded because the tail number is the checkable core of the surfacing footage and it checks out: the aircraft exists, is a King Air, and is certificated for weather modification. That establishes what the plane is licensed to do, not what it was carrying on any given flight. The restricted category is a certification class, not evidence of an undisclosed payload. The Fargo address is shared by several aviation businesses (Fargo Jet Center, SFH Inc), so co-location is corroborating, not conclusive, on operator identity.
